source_text: Sed qui dixerat: Petite et accipietis, petentibus dederat eum exitum quem quisque desiderauerat. Nam, si quando inter se de martyrii sui uoto sermocinabantur, Saturninus quidem omnibus bestiis uelle se obici profitebatur, ut scilicet gloriosiorem gestaret coronam. Itaque in commissione spectaculi ipse et Reuocatus leopardum experti etiam super pulpitum ab urso uexati sunt. Saturus autem nihil magis quam ursum abominabatur; sed uno morsu leopardi confici se iam praesumebat. Itaque cum apro subministraretur, uenator potius qui illum ad aprum subligauerat, subfossus ab eadem bestia post dies muneris obiit; Saturus solummodo tractus est. Et cum ad ursum substrictus esset in ponte, ursus de cauea prodire noluit. Itaque secundo Saturus inlaesus reuocatur.
pass_a_gloss: But the one who had said 'ask and you will receive' had given to those asking that end which each one had desired. For if ever they talked among themselves about their vow concerning their martyrdom, Saturninus indeed kept professing that he wanted to be exposed to all the beasts, namely so that he might wear a more glorious crown. Therefore in the staging of the spectacle he and Revocatus met a leopard and were also mauled on the platform by a bear. Saturus detested nothing more than a bear, but was already expecting that he would be dispatched by one bite of a leopard. So when he was furnished to the boar, instead the hunter who had tied him to the boar, gored underneath by the same beast, died after the days of the games; Saturus was only dragged. And when he had been bound on the bridge for the bear, the bear refused to come out of the cage. So for a second time Saturus is called back unharmed.
pass_b_english: But he who had said, 'Ask and you shall receive' (John 16:24), had granted to those who asked the end that each one had longed for. For whenever they talked together about their prayer concerning their martyrdom, Saturninus declared that he wished to be cast before all the beasts, so that he might wear a more glorious crown. So when the spectacle was put on, he and Revocatus faced a leopard and were also attacked by a bear upon the platform.

Saturus, however, dreaded nothing more than a bear, but he fully expected to be finished by a single bite of a leopard. So when he was delivered to the boar, it was rather the huntsman who had fastened him to the boar who, gored by the same beast, died after the days of the games, while Saturus was merely dragged. And when he had been bound on the bridge for the bear, the bear would not come out of its cage. So Saturus was called back a second time unhurt.

choices.why: exitum here means the manner and result of their encounter with the beasts, not merely death or departure, as shown by the following contrasting beast episodes.

choices.english: at the staging of the show
choices.why: ablative of time or circumstance with commissio as the formal putting-on of games, and spectaculum as the arena entertainment.
rejected: in the commission of the spectacle

choices.why: super with accusative of place where they were exposed and mauled, referring to the raised structure in the arena.
